title.zh: 卷266 列傳五十三 葉方蔼 沈荃 励杜讷 徐元珙 许三礼 王士祯 韩菼 汤右会
title.en: Volume 266 Biographies 53: Ye Fangai, Shen Quan, Li Du Ne, Xu Yuangong, Xu Sanli, Wang Shizhen, Han Tan, Tang Youhui
title.raw: 卷266 列傳五十三 葉方蔼 沈荃 励杜讷 徐元珙 许三礼 王士祯 韩菼 汤右会

sentences.zh: 列傳五十三

translations.literal: Biographies 53
translations.idiomatic: Biography 53

sentences.zh: 葉方藹，字子吉，江南崑山人。

translations.literal: Ye Fangai, courtesy name Ziji, was a native of Kunshan in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Fangai, whose courtesy name was Ziji, came from Kunshan in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi he placed third among the top three graduates of the jinshi examination and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 (1659) he took third place among the top three jinshi graduates and received appointment as a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 江南奏銷案起，坐奪官。

translations.literal: When the Jiangnan tax-report case arose, he was stripped of office for his involvement.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangnan tax-report scandal broke, he lost his post on that account.

sentences.zh: 尋授上林苑蕃育署丞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed deputy director of the Breeding Office in the Imperial Parks.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the post of deputy director at the Imperial Parks Breeding Office.

sentences.zh: 事白，還故官。

translations.literal: When the matter was cleared, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Once the affair was cleared, he returned to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi he served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Activities.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 (1673) he became a Daily Lecturer and Recorder of the Emperor's Activities.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷國子監司業，再遷侍講。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, and again promoted to Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he rose to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, then again to Court Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 宴瀛台，群臣皆進詩賦，方藹制八箴以獻，上甚悅，命撰太極圖論以進，賜貂裘、文綺。

translations.literal: At a banquet on Yingtai Terrace all the ministers presented poems; Fangai composed eight admonitions to present, which greatly pleased the emperor, who ordered him to draft an essay on the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate and rewarded him with a sable coat and patterned silk.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet on Yingtai Terrace the court presented verse; Fangai offered eight admonitions that delighted the emperor, who ordered him to compose a treatise on the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate and gave him a sable coat and brocade.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷左庶子，再遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Left Sub-Reader, then again to Court Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became Left Sub-Reader, then Court Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命充孝經衍義總裁，進講通鑑。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was ordered to serve as chief editor of the Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety and to lecture on the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was put in charge of the Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety and lectured on the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 上問：「諸葛亮何如伊尹？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "How does Zhuge Liang compare with Yi Yin?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How does Zhuge Liang compare with Yi Yin?"

sentences.zh: 」方藹對曰：「伊尹聖人，可比孔子；

translations.literal: " Fangai replied: "Yi Yin was a sage and may be compared with Confucius;
translations.idiomatic: " Fangai answered, "Yi Yin was a sage, comparable to Confucius;

sentences.zh: 諸葛亮大賢，可比顏淵。

translations.literal: Zhuge Liang was a great worthy and may be compared with Yan Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Liang was a great worthy, comparable to Yan Yuan."

sentences.zh: 」上首肯。

translations.literal: " The emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 講中庸，上問：「知行孰重？

translations.literal: While lecturing on the Doctrine of the Mean, the emperor asked: "Which is more important, knowing or acting?"
translations.idiomatic: During a lecture on the Doctrine of the Mean the emperor asked which mattered more, knowledge or action.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「宋臣硃熹之說，以次序言，則知先行後；

translations.literal: " He replied: "According to the Song minister Zhu Xi's teaching, speaking in terms of sequence, knowing comes first and acting follows;
translations.idiomatic: " He said, "In Zhu Xi's terms, in order knowing comes first and acting follows;

sentences.zh: 以功夫言，則知輕行重。

translations.literal: speaking in terms of effort, knowing is lighter and acting heavier."
translations.idiomatic: but in terms of effort, knowing weighs less and acting more."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「畢竟行重，若不能行，知亦虛知耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "After all, acting is heavier; if one cannot act, knowing is only empty knowing."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "In the end action is heavier; without action, knowledge is hollow."

sentences.zh: 」轉侍讀學士。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then made Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 十七年，充鑑古輯覽、皇輿表總裁，經筵講官，直南書房。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he served as chief editor of the Mirror of Antiquity and the Imperial Territory Tables, as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and was assigned to the Southern Studios.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he headed the Mirror of Antiquity and Imperial Territory Tables, lectured at the Classics Colloquium, and served in the Southern Studios.

sentences.zh: 上勤於典學，故事，以大臣二人日直，上特以屬方藹，兼掌院學士，兼禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was diligent in classical learning; by precedent two grand ministers took daily duty, but the emperor specially entrusted this to Fangai alone, while he also held the posts of Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor studied the classics tirelessly; though two grand ministers normally shared daily duty, he entrusted Fangai alone, who also served as Hanlin Chancellor and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十八年，召試博學宏詞，命方藹閱卷，總裁明史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, at the special examination for erudite scholars, he was ordered to grade papers and to serve as chief editor of the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, at the erudition examination, he graded papers and headed the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 十九年，尚書講義成。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Exegesis of the Documents was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the Exegesis of the Documents was finished.

sentences.zh: 上以講幄勞，加方藹尚書銜。

translations.literal: The emperor, rewarding his labors at the lecture hall, added to Fangai the titular rank of minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded his lecture-hall service by granting Fangai a ministerial title.

sentences.zh: 上講易噬嗑卦辭，方藹與同官庫勒納進所撰乾坤二卦總論，上覽竟，諭曰：「卦爻義各有不同，即如噬嗑卦中四爻主用刑者言，初上二爻主受刑者言，必得總論發揮，庶全卦之義了然，諸卦可依此撰進。

translations.literal: When the emperor lectured on the Shi He hexagram in the Changes, Fangai and his colleague Kulena submitted their general treatises on the Qian and Kun hexagrams; after reading them through, the emperor instructed: "The meaning of each line differs—as in Shi He, the four middle lines speak of those who apply punishment, while the first and top lines speak of those who receive it; a general treatise is needed to bring out the whole hexagram, and the other hexagrams should be drafted likewise."
translations.idiomatic: While lecturing on Shi He, Fangai and Kulena submitted treatises on Qian and Kun; the emperor read them and said each hexagram needs a general discussion—Shi He's middle lines concern those who punish, the first and last those punished—and the rest should follow this pattern.

sentences.zh: 」二十年，授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: " In the twentieth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twentieth year he became Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，卒，遣奠茶酒，賜白金二百。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died; the court sent offerings of tea and wine and granted two hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he died; the court sent tea and wine for the obsequies and two hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 上以方藹久侍講幄，啟沃勤勞，命優恤，賜諡文敏。

translations.literal: Because Fangai had long served at the lecture hall with devoted counsel, the emperor ordered special condolence payments and bestowed the posthumous title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: For his long service and devoted counsel at the lecture hall, the emperor ordered special mourning gifts and the posthumous title Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 方藹初釋褐，以文章受知世祖。

translations.literal: When Fangai first left office after the examination, he won Shizu recognition through his literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: When Fangai first entered service, he won the Shunzhi emperor's favor through his writing.

sentences.zh: 家居時，有密陳其居鄉不法者，下其事江蘇巡撫田雯覈覆。

translations.literal: While at home someone secretly reported his misconduct in the countryside, and the matter was referred to Jiangsu Governor Tian Wen for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: At home a secret denunciation accused him of local misconduct, and the case went to Jiangsu Governor Tian Wen.

sentences.zh: 雯以鄉評入告，上曰：「朕固知方藹不如是也！

translations.literal: Wen reported the local opinion, and the emperor said: "I have always known Fangai is not like that!"
translations.idiomatic: Wen reported local opinion, and the emperor said, "I have always known Fangai is not such a man!"

sentences.zh: 」其後事聖祖，直內廷，眷遇優渥。

translations.literal: " Thereafter serving the Kangxi emperor in the inner court, he enjoyed exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: " He later served the Kangxi emperor in the inner court with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 方藹故廉謹，其卒，以板扉為臥榻，支以四甕，布帳多補綴，無以為斂，見者以為難能。

translations.literal: Fangai had always been frugal and careful; at his death his bed was a plank door propped on four jars, his cloth curtains much patched, and there was nothing for burial—observers regarded this as hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal by nature, at death he slept on a plank propped on four jars, patched curtains, nothing for burial—onlookers called it rare integrity.

sentences.zh: 沈荃，字貞蕤，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: Shen Quan, courtesy name Zhenrui, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Quan, courtesy name Zhenrui, came from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治九年一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he placed third among the top three jinshi graduates and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 (1652) he took third among the top three jinshi and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 世祖擇翰林官外轉，荃出為大樑道副使。

translations.literal: Shizu selected Hanlin officials for outside transfer, and Quan went out as Vice Commissioner of the Daliang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi emperor rotated Hanlin men outward; Quan became Vice Commissioner of the Daliang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 劇盜董天祿、牛光天剽掠許、潁間，荃督兵捕治，殲其渠，群盜皆散去。

translations.literal: The bandit chiefs Dong Tianlu and Niu Guangtian plundered between Xu and Ying; Quan led troops to capture them, destroyed their leaders, and the band dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits Dong Tianlu and Niu Guangtian raided Xu and Ying; Quan destroyed their leaders and the gangs scattered.

sentences.zh: 禹州盜倚竹園為巢，殺人越貨，荃遣吏卒收捕，發土得屍十餘，悉按誅之。

translations.literal: At Yuzhou bandits used Bamboo Garden as a lair, killing and robbing; Quan sent officers to seize them, dug up more than ten corpses, and executed all according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou bandits nested at Bamboo Garden; Quan seized them, unearthed a dozen corpses, and executed all by law.

sentences.zh: 尋署按察使，疏言：「師方南征，必經南陽、汝寧諸府，供應疲苦，亢村、郭店諸驛，官死夫逃，請敕均撥驛站銀兩。

translations.literal: Soon acting as Surveillance Commissioner, he memorialized: "The army is marching south and must pass Nanyang and Runing; supply stations are exhausted—at Kangcun and Guodian officials and couriers have died or fled—please order equal distribution of courier funds."
translations.idiomatic: As acting Surveillance Commissioner he wrote: the southern campaign will pass Nanyang and Runing; courier stations are broken—please redistribute funds.

sentences.zh: 師既入楚，留馬彰德，役民飼秣，請敕以懷慶、衛輝、廣平、順德、大名諸府更番分駐。

translations.literal: After the army entered Chu, horses were left at Zhangde and the people fed fodder—please rotate garrisons among Huaiqing, Weihui, Guangping, Shunde, and Daming.
translations.idiomatic: After the army entered Chu, horses stayed at Zhangde burdening the people—please rotate troops among five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 各縣常平倉蓄穀太寡，請敕定額：大縣五六百石，小縣三四百石。

translations.literal: Granaries in each county held too little grain—please fix quotas: five to six hundred piculs for large counties, three to four hundred for small ones.
translations.idiomatic: County granaries were too low—he asked fixed quotas of five to six hundred piculs for large counties, three to four for small.

sentences.zh: 開封自河決後，城垣淤圮，官吏分駐各邑，鄉闈暫移輝縣。

translations.literal: After the Yellow River burst, Kaifeng's walls were silted and ruined; officials were scattered and the provincial exam moved to Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yellow River flood Kaifeng's walls collapsed; officials scattered and exams moved to Huixian.

sentences.zh: 近奉旨修復汴城，請敕籌撥錢糧，督倡興工。

translations.literal: Recently ordered to restore Bian city—please allocate funds and urge the work.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to rebuild Bian city—he asked funds and supervision.

sentences.zh: 河南土地，原有上中下等則，向因疆井混淆，一例派糧。

translations.literal: Henan land had upper, middle, and lower grades, but boundaries had been confused and grain levied uniformly.
translations.idiomatic: Henan land had three grades, but confused boundaries led to uniform levies.

sentences.zh: 今查勘漸定，請敕視萬曆年間則例，照地派糧。

translations.literal: Now surveys are settled—please levy by Wanli-era rates according to the land.
translations.idiomatic: Surveys settled—please levy by Wanli rates by land quality.

sentences.zh: 河南兵額一萬二千，奉旨缺額免補，有汰無增，駐防分汛，每苦不足，請敕仍許募補足額。

translations.literal: Henan's quota was twelve thousand troops; vacancies were not filled though garrisons lacked men—please allow recruitment to full strength.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve thousand troops were authorized but vacancies unfilled while garrisons lacked men—please allow recruitment.

sentences.zh: 」俱下部議行。

translations.literal: " All were referred to the ministries for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " All were sent to the ministries for action.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，以憂歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he returned home on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 he went home for mourning.

sentences.zh: 六年，授直隸通薊道，坐事左遷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Tongji Circuit in Zhili, then demoted for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he took Tongji Circuit in Zhili, then was demoted.

sentences.zh: 九年，授浙江寧波同知。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Ningbo Sub-Prefect in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Ningbo Sub-Prefect in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 未上官，特旨召對，命作各體書，稱旨，詔以原品內用。

translations.literal: Before taking office he was specially summoned, ordered to write in every script style, pleased the emperor, and was ordered to serve at his former rank within the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before reporting he was summoned, wrote all scripts to the emperor's liking, and was kept at his former rank in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十年，授侍講，直南書房。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made Court Lecturer and assigned to the Southern Studios.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became Court Lecturer in the Southern Studios.

sentences.zh: 十一年，轉侍讀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he became Reader.

sentences.zh: 十二年，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was Daily Lecturer and Recorder.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷少詹事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢詹事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became Mentor.

sentences.zh: 十八年，旱，求直言。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, during drought, the emperor sought frank counsel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, amid drought, the emperor called for frank speech.

sentences.zh: 時更定新例，罪人當流者徙烏喇，下廷臣議。

translations.literal: New regulations then provided that those liable to exile should be sent to Wula; the court debated.
translations.idiomatic: New rules sent exiles to Wula; the court debated.

sentences.zh: 荃謂：「烏喇去蒙古三四千里，地極寒，人畜多凍死。

translations.literal: Quan said: "Wula lies three or four thousand li from Mongolia; the land is bitterly cold and men and beasts often freeze to death."
translations.idiomatic: Quan said Wula was three or four thousand li away, bitterly cold, and many froze to death.

sentences.zh: 今罪不至死者，乃遣流，而更驅之死地，宜如舊例便。

translations.literal: Those whose crime does not merit death are now exiled only to be driven to their deaths—it is better to keep the old rule."
translations.idiomatic: Sending non-capital offenders there drives them to death—the old rule is better."

sentences.zh: 」疏上，有旨令畫一，荃持前議益堅，且曰：「此議行，三日不雨者，甘服欺罔罪。

translations.literal: " When the memorial went up the emperor ordered uniformity; Quan held his view more firmly and said: "If this rule is adopted and it does not rain within three days, I will gladly accept the crime of deception."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered uniformity; Quan insisted and wagered rain within three days or deception.

sentences.zh: 」上改容納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor's expression changed and he accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor relented and accepted.

sentences.zh: 越二日，天竟雨，例得罷。

translations.literal: Two days later rain actually fell and the regulation was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later it rained and the rule was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十九年，上以講幄勞，加荃禮部侍郎銜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the emperor, rewarding lecture-hall service, added Quan the titular rank of Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the emperor gave Quan a Vice Minister of Rites title for lecture service.

sentences.zh: 二十一年正月，乾清宮宴廷臣，賦柏梁體詩，荃與焉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-first year, at a banquet in the Hall of Mental Cultivation the ministers composed Bo Liang-style verse; Quan took part.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year's first month Quan joined a Bo Liang verse banquet at the Hall of Mental Cultivation.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he died.

sentences.zh: 上以荃貧，賜白金五百。

translations.literal: Because Quan was poor, the emperor granted five hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Finding him poor, the emperor gave five hundred taels.

sentences.zh: 子宗敬，二十七年進士，改庶吉士，以編修入直，上命作書，因諭大學士李光地曰：「朕初學書，宗敬父荃指陳得失。

translations.literal: His son Zongjing passed the jinshi in the twenty-seventh year, became a bachelor, and entered service as compiler; ordered to write, the emperor told Grand Secretary Li Guangdi: "When I first studied calligraphy, Zongjing's father Quan pointed out my faults."
translations.idiomatic: Son Zongjing, jinshi in year 27, became compiler; the emperor told Li Guangdi that Quan had corrected his early calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 至今作字，未嘗不思其勤也。

translations.literal: Even now when I write I never forget his diligence."
translations.idiomatic: He said he still remembers Quan's diligence when writing."

sentences.zh: 」宗敬官至太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: " Zongjing rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: " Zongjing reached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 勵杜訥，字近公，直隸靜海人。

translations.literal: Li Dune, courtesy name Jingong, was a native of Jinghai in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dune, courtesy name Jingong, came from Jinghai in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 勵氏自鎮海北遷，訥以杜姓補諸生。

translations.literal: The Li clan had moved north from Zhenhai; Dune entered school under the surname Du.
translations.idiomatic: The Lis had moved from Zhenhai; Dune studied as a Du.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，纂世祖實錄，選善書之士，訥試第一，赴館繕錄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, compiling the Veritable Records of Shizu, skilled calligraphers were chosen; Dune ranked first and went to the project.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2, compiling Shizu's Veritable Records, Dune ranked first among calligraphers.

sentences.zh: 書成敘勞，授福建福寧州同，命留直南書房，食六品俸。

translations.literal: When the work was done he was appointed Tongzhi of Funing in Fujian but kept at the Southern Studios on sixth-rank salary.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded for the work, he was named Funing Tongzhi but kept in the Southern Studios at sixth rank.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授編修，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was made compiler and Daily Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became compiler and Daily Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，奏請復勵姓。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he memorialized to restore the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he asked to restore the Li surname.

sentences.zh: 聖祖方閱通鑑綱目，杜訥與學士張英侍，閱竟，杜訥請以御批宣示史館，下禮部翰林院會議，如所請。

translations.literal: While the emperor read the Outline of the Comprehensive Mirror, Du Ne and Academician Zhang Ying attended; when finished Du Ne asked that imperial comments be shown to the Historiography Office—the ministries agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the Mirror's outline with Zhang Ying, Du Ne asked imperial glosses go to the Historiography Office—approved.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷贊善。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he became Tutor.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷侍講，改光祿寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Court Lecturer and made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he became Court Lecturer and Vice Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，遷通政司參議。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he was transferred to Censor of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year he became Transmission Censor.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，遷太僕寺卿，再遷宗人府府丞。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred to Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he headed the Imperial Stud, then the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he became Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「督撫大吏，朝廷畀以百餘城吏治、數千里民生，責任至重；

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Governors-general and governors hold over a hundred prefectures and thousands of li of people's livelihood—the responsibility is weighty;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote that governors held vast territories and heavy responsibility;

sentences.zh: 若託詞鎮靜，漸成悠忽，不過以期會簿書忝封疆之寄。

translations.literal: if they plead calm and grow negligent, meeting deadlines on documents only dishonors their charge."
translations.idiomatic: pleading calm while neglecting duty dishonors their trust."

sentences.zh: 請敕各督撫年終匯奏若何察吏安民、興利除弊，以備清覽；

translations.literal: Please order each governor to report yearly how he inspected officials, settled the people, and advanced or removed abuses for imperial review;
translations.idiomatic: He asked yearly reports on inspecting officials and benefiting the people;

sentences.zh: 不實，則治以欺罔之罪：庶時時警勉，不敢優游草率，貽誤地方。

translations.literal: false reports to be punished as deception, so they would not be lax and harm the regions."
translations.idiomatic: false ones punished as deception to prevent lax rule."

sentences.zh: 籓司專掌錢穀，臬司專掌刑名，州縣之錢糧有無虧空，定案之爰書有無駁審，詳實並列，則籓臬之優劣亦無遁情。

translations.literal: The provincial treasurer handles revenue, the provincial judge criminal matters—listing county deficits and appealed cases would expose their merit."
translations.idiomatic: Listing revenue deficits and appealed cases would reveal treasurer and judge quality."

sentences.zh: 」議如所請。

translations.literal: " The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " Adopted.

sentences.zh: 又言：「提鎮保送將弁，時有騎射甚劣並年老之員，經特旨甄別。

translations.literal: He also said: "Generals recommending officers sometimes sent poor archers or aged men, whom the emperor had specially screened."
translations.idiomatic: He noted generals sometimes recommended poor archers or old men already screened.

sentences.zh: 典戎要務，首在考察將弁，請敕部將各提鎮所屬引見不稱旨之員，匯冊呈覽，並定處分。

translations.literal: Military affairs depend on inspecting officers—please have the ministry compile those who failed audience and fix penalties."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the ministry compile failed candidates and set penalties."

sentences.zh: 」下詔所司飭行。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered enforcement.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered enforcement.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was promoted Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he became Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 杜訥學行醇粹，直禁廷二十餘年，無纖芥過失。

translations.literal: Du Ne's learning and conduct were pure; twenty years in the forbidden precinct without the slightest fault.
translations.idiomatic: Pure in learning and conduct, he served the inner court twenty years without fault.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，上駐蹕靜海，敕獎杜訥謹慎勤勞，親定諡曰文恪，手書賜其家。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, while the emperor was at Jinghai, he praised Du Ne's diligence, fixed the posthumous title Wenkai, and wrote it for the family.
translations.idiomatic: In year 44 at Jinghai the emperor praised him, set posthumous Wenkai, and wrote it himself.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng 1 posthumously made him Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 八年，祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was enshrined in the Temple of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he entered the Temple of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，加贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: When Gaozong acceded, he was further posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong further posthumously made him Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子廷儀，字南湖。

translations.literal: His son Tingyi, courtesy name Nanhu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tingyi, courtesy name Nanhu.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十九年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi and became a bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 39 he passed the jinshi and entered the Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，特命直南書房。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was specially ordered to the Southern Studios.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he was specially assigned to the Southern Studios.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，授編修，遭父喪，既終，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was appointed compiler; after his father's mourning ended he served as Daily Lecturer and Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he became compiler; after mourning he was Daily Lecturer and Recorder.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士，充經筵講官，擢翰林院掌院學士、兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose through Grand Secretary, Classics Colloquium lecturer, to Hanlin Chancellor and Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Secretary, Classics lecturer, Hanlin Chancellor, and Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 1 he became Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 疏言各省常平倉穀，當責督撫覈實盤查，年終冊報；

translations.literal: He memorialized that each province's ever-normal granary grain should be verified by governors and reported yearly;
translations.idiomatic: He asked governors to audit ever-normal granaries and report yearly;

sentences.zh: 又請於古北口外設理事同知，檢察命、盜獄：並從之。

translations.literal: he also asked to set a supervising sub-prefect beyond the ancient northern pass to inspect life-and-death and theft cases: all approved.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked a sub-prefect beyond the pass to inspect capital cases—all approved.

sentences.zh: 二年，疏言各州縣團練民壯，當選習槍箭，勤加訓練，上韙之，下直省督撫實力奉行；

translations.literal: In the second year he said local militia should drill with firearms; the emperor approved and ordered governors to enforce;
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he urged militia firearms drill; the emperor ordered enforcement;

sentences.zh: 又疏請分立內外監，內監居要犯，外監居輕犯，別為女監，另牆隔別：均報可。

translations.literal: he also asked separate inner and outer prisons, a women's prison walled apart: all approved.
translations.idiomatic: he asked separate inner, outer, and women's prisons—all approved.

sentences.zh: 迭疏論監生考職，禁止私鹽，清查入官家產，各舉其叢弊所在，並下部議行。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized on examination of purchased degrees, private salt, and confiscated estates, exposing abuses; all referred to ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed abuses in purchased degrees, private salt, and confiscated property—sent to ministries.

sentences.zh: 七年，加太子太傅，賜「矜慎平恕」榜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the plaque "Prudent, Calm, Fair, and Forgiving."
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he became Grand Tutor and received the plaque Prudent, Calm, Fair, and Forgiving.

sentences.zh: 九年，調吏部，仍專管刑部事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to Personnel but still oversaw Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he moved to Personnel while still handling Justice.

sentences.zh: 十年，卒，諡文恭。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died with posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he died; posthumous Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子宗萬，字滋大。

translations.literal: His son Zongwan, courtesy name Zida.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongwan, courtesy name Zida.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Kangxi he passed the jinshi, became a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 60 he passed the jinshi, became bachelor and compiler.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，命直南書房，充日講起居注官，督山西學政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng he was ordered to the Southern Studios, Daily Lecturer, and Educational Commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzheng 2: Southern Studios, Daily Lecturer, Shanxi Educational Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷國子監司業，按試潞安。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and examined Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he became Vice Director of Education and examined Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 臨晉民解進朝詐稱御前總管，私書請託，宗萬疏發之，諭嘉獎，遷侍讀，命巡察山西。

translations.literal: At Linjin a man falsely claimed to be an imperial chief eunuch and solicited favors; Zongwan exposed him, won praise, became Reader, and was ordered to inspect Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At Linjin he exposed a fraud posing as an imperial eunuch, was praised, made Reader, and inspected Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 八年，巡撫石麟劾宗萬擾驛遞，並縱僕受賕，坐奪官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Governor Shi Lin impeached Zongwan for disturbing couriers and tolerating bribe-taking servants; he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Governor Shi Lin impeached him for courier abuse and servants' bribes; he lost office.

sentences.zh: 十年，起鴻臚寺少卿，仍直南書房。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was restored as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Banquets and returned to the Southern Studios.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was restored as Vice Director of Imperial Banquets and the Southern Studios.

sentences.zh: 四遷至禮部侍郎，調刑部。

translations.literal: After four promotions he reached Vice Minister of Rites, then was transferred to Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of Rites, then Justice.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，吏部劾宗萬保舉河員受請託，坐奪官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong Personnel impeached Zongwan for recommending a river official who took bribes; he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 1: impeached for a bribed river recommendation; stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 尋命直武英殿。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon assigned to the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 七年，再起侍講學士，累遷通政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again made Reader-in-Waiting and rose to Transmission Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was Reader-in-Waiting again and rose to Transmission Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 直懋勤殿，纂秘殿珠林，遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: Assigned to the Hall of Earnest Diligence to compile the Secret Hall Pearl Forest, then Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hall of Earnest Diligence he compiled the Pearl Forest, then became Left Vice Censor.

sentences.zh: 擢工部侍郎，調刑部。

translations.literal: Promoted Vice Minister of Works, then transferred to Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Works, then Justice.

sentences.zh: 十年，坐縱門客生事，复奪官，手詔詰責，命還裡閉戶讀書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, for tolerating a client's misconduct, he was again stripped; the emperor wrote reproof and ordered him home to study.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, tolerating a client's abuse, he was stripped again and sent home to study.

sentences.zh: 督撫那蘇圖劾宗萬縱弟佔官地，命承修固安城工，免其罪。

translations.literal: Governor Na Sutu impeached him for letting his brother seize official land; he was ordered to repair the Gu'an city works to clear the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Na Sutu impeached his brother's land seizure; he repaired Gu'an walls to clear it.

sentences.zh: 十六年，復起侍講學士，累遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was again made Reader-in-Waiting and rose to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he was Reader-in-Waiting again and rose to Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he died.

sentences.zh: 子守謙，嘉慶十年進士，官編修。

translations.literal: His son Shouqian passed the jinshi in the tenth year of Jiaqing and served as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shouqian, jinshi Jiaqing 10, became compiler.

sentences.zh: 自杜訥以諸生受知遇，子孫繼起，四世皆入翰林。

translations.literal: From Du Ne as a student gaining favor, his descendants rose in succession—four generations entered the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: From Du Ne's rise as a student, four generations entered the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 徐元珙，字輯五，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Xu Yuangong, courtesy name Jiwu, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuangong, courtesy name Jiwu, came from Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，授刑部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi and was appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Justice, then promoted to department director.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 12 jinshi; Justice clerk, then department director.

sentences.zh: 典廣西試，遷郎中。

translations.literal: He conducted the Guangxi examination and was transferred to division director.
translations.idiomatic: He examined Guangxi and became division director.

sentences.zh: 出為福建建寧道僉事，善治盜。

translations.literal: Going out as Fujian Jianning Circuit Commissioner, he was skilled at suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: As Fujian Jianning Commissioner he excelled at suppressing bandits.

sentences.zh: 移山西冀寧南道參議，遭母憂去。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shanxi Jining South Circuit Commissioner, he left on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Shanxi Jining South Commissioner; left for mourning.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，起直隸口北道參議。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi he was recalled as Koubei Circuit Commissioner in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 12 he returned as Koubei Commissioner in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 時宣鎮未設府縣，但置同知分防。

translations.literal: The Xuan garrison had no prefecture or county, only sub-prefects for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had no prefecture—only sub-prefects for defense.

sentences.zh: 元珙和調將士，嚴斥堠，增亭障，葺城郭，修學舍，邊境晏然。

translations.literal: Yuangong harmonized troops, strengthened watch-posts, added barriers, repaired walls and schools, and the border was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He harmonized troops, strengthened posts and walls, repaired schools, and pacified the border.

sentences.zh: 入為光祿寺少卿，歷太僕寺卿、通政使。

translations.literal: Entering the capital he became Vice Director of Imperial Entertainments, then Director of the Imperial Stud and Transmission Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he was Vice Director of Entertainments, then Stud Director and Transmission Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he became Director of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 疏請釐正北郊配饗位次，略言：「本朝分祭南北郊。

translations.literal: He memorialized to correct the northern suburban accompanying sacrifices, saying: "This dynasty sacrifices separately at the southern and northern suburbs."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to fix northern suburban sacrifices: this dynasty separates south and north.

sentences.zh: 圜丘南鄉，三聖並配，甚鉅典也。

translations.literal: At the Round Mound facing south the Three Sages accompany—a great rite.
translations.idiomatic: At the Round Mound facing south the Three Sages accompany—a supreme rite.

sentences.zh: 獨方澤配位，臣不能無議。

translations.literal: Only at the Square Mound accompanying positions, I cannot refrain from objection.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the Square Mound I must object to the accompanying positions.

sentences.zh: 昭穆之位，分左右不分東西。

translations.literal: Zhao and Mu positions are divided left and right, not east and west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Mu are left and right, not east and west.

sentences.zh: 圜丘南鄉，則東為左為昭，西為右為穆；

translations.literal: At the Round Mound facing south, east is left as Zhao and west right as Mu;
translations.idiomatic: Facing south at the Round Mound, east is Zhao left and west Mu right;

sentences.zh: 地祇既北鄉，則西為左為昭，東為右為穆。

translations.literal: the Earth Spirit facing north makes west left as Zhao and east right as Mu.
translations.idiomatic: the Earth Spirit facing north makes west Zhao and east Mu.

sentences.zh: 蓋東西有定方，而左右無定位，從正位所鄉而殊。

translations.literal: East and west have fixed directions while left and right have no fixed place—they differ according to the main position faced.
translations.idiomatic: East and west are fixed; left and right shift with the main altar's orientation.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐地祇皆南鄉，至宋政和四年，引北牖答陰之義，始改北鄉，配位亦改焉。

translations.literal: Han and Tang earth sacrifices faced south; in Song Zhenghe 4, citing answering yin through the northern window, they turned north and accompanying positions changed.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Tang faced south; Song Zhenghe 4 turned north and changed accompaniments.

sentences.zh: 明嘉靖九年，建方澤壇，因宋制，地祇北鄉，而配位仍設於東，不應古禮。

translations.literal: Ming Jiajing 9 built the Square Mound following Song; earth faced north but accompaniments stayed east, not matching ancient rites.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Jiajing followed Song; earth faced north but accompaniments stayed east—wrong.

sentences.zh: 蓋其時禮官誤執以東為左，因循至今。

translations.literal: Ritual officers wrongly held east as left and this has continued.
translations.idiomatic: Officers mistook east for left and the error persisted.

sentences.zh: 然明配位止一太祖，或左或右，尚無越次之嫌。

translations.literal: Yet in Ming there was only Taizu as accompaniment, left or right without crossing order.
translations.idiomatic: Ming had only Taizu; left or right did not disturb order.

sentences.zh: 今三聖並配，左右易位，因之昭穆失序；

translations.literal: Now three sages accompany together and left and right swap, so Zhao and Mu lose order;
translations.idiomatic: Now three sages accompany and swap places, disordering Zhao and Mu;

sentences.zh: 況配位誤則從壇皆誤，即陵山從祀嶽鎮者亦誤。

translations.literal: moreover if accompaniment is wrong the altar is wrong, and even mountain sacrifices to peaks are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: wrong accompaniment corrupts the altar and peak sacrifices too.

sentences.zh: 揆諸典禮，實有未安，有待釐正。

translations.literal: Weighing the canonical rites, this is truly unsettled and awaits correction.
translations.idiomatic: By canonical rites it is unsettled and needs correction.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下廷臣集議，學士徐乾學、韓菼皆韙元珙議，獨許三禮駁之，遂不行。

translations.literal: " The memorial went in; the court debated; Academicians Xu Qianxue and Han Tan approved Yuangong's view; only Xu Sanli objected, so it was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " Debated; Xu Qianxue and Han Tan agreed; Xu Sanli objected—it was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 語見三禮傳。

translations.literal: See the biography of Xu Sanli.
translations.idiomatic: See Xu Sanli's biography.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he became Left Vice Censor.

sentences.zh: 疏請正北海祀典，略言：「唐望祭洛州，即今河南府。

translations.literal: He memorialized to rectify the northern sea sacrifice, saying: "Tang looked to Luozhou, which is present-day Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to fix the northern sea rite: Tang looked to Luozhou, today's Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋望祭孟州，即今懷慶府。

translations.literal: Song looked to Mengzhou, which is present-day Huaiqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Song looked to Mengzhou, today's Huaiqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明依宋制。

translations.literal: Ming followed the Song system.
translations.idiomatic: Ming followed Song.

sentences.zh: 說者謂懷慶屬濟源，潛通北海，故於此望祭焉。

translations.literal: Some say because Huaiqing belongs to Jiyuan and secretly connects to the northern sea, sacrifice is made there.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Huaiqing links to Jiyuan and the northern sea—hence sacrifice there.

sentences.zh: 本朝定制，東海祀萊州，南海祀廣州，西海祀蒲州，皆為允當。

translations.literal: This dynasty's fixed practice sacrifices to the eastern sea at Laizhou, southern sea at Guangzhou, western sea at Puzhou—all fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern sea at Laizhou, southern at Guangzhou, western at Puzhou—all fitting.

sentences.zh: 獨北海仍祀懷慶，竊以嶽鎮方位，當準皇都。

translations.literal: Only the northern sea still sacrifices at Huaiqing; I venture that peak directions should follow the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Only the northern sea remains at Huaiqing; directions should follow the capital.

sentences.zh: 往南祭北，於義未愜。

translations.literal: Sacrificing north while facing south is unsatisfying in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificing north while the capital faces south is unsatisfying.

sentences.zh: 謹按北鎮醫巫閭山在今奉天府境，山既為北鎮，川即可為北海，矧長白山水、黑龍、鴨綠諸江，悉朝宗於海。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that Yiwulü Mountain, the northern peak, lies in present-day Fengtian; the mountain being the northern peak, its streams may serve as the northern sea, especially as Changbai waters, the Amur, and Yalu all pay homage to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwulü in Fengtian is the northern peak; its streams and rivers pay homage to the sea.

sentences.zh: 請更定北海之祭，就北鎮醫巫閭為便。

translations.literal: Please fix the northern sea sacrifice at Yiwulü for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Please fix the northern sea sacrifice at Yiwulü.

sentences.zh: 或疑歷時已久，不可輒更。

translations.literal: Some doubt that long-standing custom cannot be changed lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Some fear long custom cannot change lightly.

sentences.zh: 臣按北岳祀恆山曲陽，積二千餘年，用科臣言改祀渾源州。

translations.literal: I note the northern peak was sacrificed at Hengshan in Quyang for over two thousand years, then changed to Hunyuan on a censor's advice.
translations.idiomatic: Hengshan at Quyang for two millennia changed to Hunyuan on advice.

sentences.zh: 岳祭可更，何疑海祭？

translations.literal: If a peak sacrifice can change, why doubt changing the sea sacrifice?"
translations.idiomatic: If a peak can change, why not the sea?"

sentences.zh: 」疏入，議行。

translations.literal: " The memorial went in and was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " Adopted.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，疏乞歸養。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he asked to return home and care for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he asked to retire and care for his father.

sentences.zh: 至家，父已前卒。

translations.literal: At home his father had already died.
translations.idiomatic: At home his father was already dead.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，孝莊文皇后崩，赴闕哭臨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, when Empress Dowager Xiaozhuang died, he went to the capital to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27, at Xiaozhuang's death, he went to court to mourn.

sentences.zh: 疾作，卒於京師，上聞而憫之，喪歸，許馳驛，卹如禮。

translations.literal: Illness seized him and he died in the capital; the emperor pitied him, allowed courier service for the funeral, and mourned according to rites.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died in the capital; the emperor pitied him and granted courier funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 元珙尚風義，座主陳彩沒，妻妾繼逝，撫其一歲孤併其女，為營婚嫁，與己子無異。

translations.literal: Yuangong valued righteousness; when his patron Chen Cai died and wife and concubines followed, he raised the one-year orphan and daughter, arranging marriages as for his own children.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Chen Cai's one-year orphan and daughter as his own and arranged their marriages.

sentences.zh: 時論推其篤厚。

translations.literal: Contemporaries praised his steadfast kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised his steadfast kindness.

sentences.zh: 彩字美公，廣東順德人。

translations.literal: Cai, courtesy name Meigong, was from Shunde in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, courtesy name Meigong, came from Shunde in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，自編修出為江南常鎮道。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the ninth year of Shunzhi; from compiler he went out as Changzhen Circuit in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 9 jinshi; from compiler to Changzhen Circuit in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，江南有大獄，諸生連染被逮，彩以輕刑全活之甚眾。

translations.literal: Early in Kangxi a great case arose in Jiangnan; many students were implicated and arrested; Cai spared many with lighter sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kangxi's Jiangnan cases caught many students; Cai spared many with lighter sentences.

sentences.zh: 許三禮，字典三，河南安陽人。

translations.literal: Xu Sanli, courtesy name Diansan, was a native of Anyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sanli, courtesy name Diansan, came from Anyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 順治十八年進士，授浙江海寧知縣。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eighteenth year of Shunzhi; appointed magistrate of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 18 jinshi; magistrate of Haining, Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 海寧地瀕海，多盜，三禮練鄉勇，嚴保甲，擒盜首硃纘之等。

translations.literal: Haining bordered the sea and had many bandits; Sanli trained militia, tightened baojia, and captured the bandit chief Zhu Zuanzhi and others.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal Haining had bandits; he trained militia and captured Zhu Zuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 益修城壕，築土城尖山、鳳凰山間，戍以土兵。

translations.literal: He further repaired walls, built an earthen fort between Jianshan and Fenghuang, and garrisoned it with local troops.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired walls, built a fort between Jianshan and Fenghuang, and garrisoned it.

sentences.zh: 築塘濬河，救災儲粟，教民以務本。

translations.literal: He built dikes, dredged rivers, stored grain for famine relief, and taught the people to attend to fundamentals.
translations.idiomatic: He built dikes, dredged rivers, stored famine grain, and taught fundamentals.

sentences.zh: 立書院，延黃宗羲主講。

translations.literal: He founded an academy and invited Huang Zongxi to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: He founded an academy and invited Huang Zongxi to lecture.

sentences.zh: 在縣八年，聲譽甚美。

translations.literal: In eight years as magistrate his reputation was excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years as magistrate won excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，行取，授福建道御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was selected and appointed Fujian Circuit Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 8 he became Fujian Circuit Censor.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「漢儒董仲舒表章六經，其言道之大原出於天，與禪宗異學專主明心者不同。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Han Ru Dong Zhongshu exalted the Six Classics; he said the great origin of the Way comes from Heaven, unlike Chan heterodoxy focusing on the mind alone."
translations.idiomatic: He said Dong Zhongshu exalted the Six Classics and Heaven as the Way's origin, unlike Chan.

sentences.zh: 故宋儒程顥有儒道本天、釋教本心之辨。

translations.literal: Therefore Song Ru Cheng Hao distinguished Confucianism's Heaven-rooted Way from Buddhism's mind-rooted teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Hao distinguished Confucian Heaven from Buddhist mind.

sentences.zh: 宜視宋時六大儒，從祀國學，進稱先賢。

translations.literal: The Six Great Ru of Song should be enshrined in the Directorate and advanced to be called sages."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the Six Great Song Ru enshrined as sages."

sentences.zh: 」下廷臣議，不果行。

translations.literal: " The court debated but did not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: " The court debated but did not adopt.

sentences.zh: 時雲、貴猶未定，三禮疏言蕩平後，察大吏宜嚴，蘇民困宜寬。

translations.literal: While Yunnan and Guizhou were still unsettled, Sanli memorialized that after pacification governors should be strict and the people's hardships treated leniently.
translations.idiomatic: While Yunnan and Guizhou were unsettled he urged strict governors and lenient people after pacification.

sentences.zh: 尋命巡視北城，太常寺卿徐元珙議北郊配位應改坐西鄉東，下廷臣集議，三禮曰：「陽生於子，極於巳，故祀天在冬至，位南郊南鄉；

translations.literal: Soon ordered to inspect the northern city; when Director Xu Yuangong debated that northern suburban accompaniments should face west and east, the court debated; Sanli said: "Yang is born at zi and peaks at si, so heaven is sacrificed at winter solstice at the southern suburb facing south;"
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting the north city, on northern suburban positions Sanli said yang from zi to si means heaven at winter solstice faces south;

sentences.zh: 陰生於午，極於亥，故祀地在夏至，位北郊北鄉。

translations.literal: yin is born at wu and peaks at hai, so earth is sacrificed at summer solstice at the northern suburb facing north.
translations.idiomatic: yin from wu to hai means earth at summer solstice faces north.

sentences.zh: 答陰答陽，義各有取。

translations.literal: Answering yin and answering yang each has its appropriate meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Answering yin and yang each has reason.

sentences.zh: 配位者主道也，義在近尊者為上。

translations.literal: Accompanying positions represent the Way; the meaning is that the nearer honored is above.
translations.idiomatic: Accompaniments represent the Way; the nearer honored is above.

sentences.zh: 故配天尚左，配地尚右，並居東。

translations.literal: Therefore accompanying heaven favors the left, accompanying earth favors the right, both placed in the east.
translations.idiomatic: So accompanying heaven favors left, earth right, both in the east.

sentences.zh: 改之非是。

translations.literal: To change is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Change is wrong.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " Adopted.

sentences.zh: 尋疏請定武臣守制例，下廷臣集議，有謂本朝無此例者。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized to fix military mourning regulations; the court debated and some said this dynasty had no such precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he asked military mourning rules; some said there was no precedent.

sentences.zh: 三禮曰：「宋高宗紹興七年，岳飛聞母訃，解兵柄徒步歸廬山，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: Sanli said: "In Song Gaozong's seventh year Yue Fei, hearing of his mother's death, laid down command and walked to Lushan, mourning at the tomb three years."
translations.idiomatic: Sanli cited Yue Fei laying down command and mourning three years at Lushan in 1137.

sentences.zh: 此往代守制例也。

translations.literal: This is the ancient military mourning precedent."
translations.idiomatic: This is the ancient military mourning precedent."

sentences.zh: 」遂定議武臣守制自此始。

translations.literal: " It was decided that military mourning began from this.
translations.idiomatic: " Military mourning was fixed from this.

sentences.zh: 旋擢通政司右參議。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted Right Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Right Transmission Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷提督四譯館、太常寺少卿，再遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to oversee the Four Translation Offices and Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices, then again to President of the Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he oversaw the Four Translation Offices, became Vice Director of Sacrifices, then Court of Revision president.

sentences.zh: 召對便殿，上曰：「河圖洛書，道治之原。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience in the side hall, the emperor said: "The River Chart and Luo Writings are the origin of the Way and governance."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, the emperor said the River Chart and Luo Writings are the origin of governance.

sentences.zh: 一二三四五，六七八九十，忽金火易位何也？

translations.literal: One two three four five, six seven eight nine ten—why do metal and fire suddenly swap positions?"
translations.idiomatic: Why do one through five and six through ten suddenly swap metal and fire?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此即一陰一陽之道也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "This is the Way of one yin and one yang."
translations.idiomatic: " He said this is the Way of one yin and one yang.

sentences.zh: 天地大德曰生，故河圖左旋，而相生為順數；

translations.literal: The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is generation; therefore the River Chart turns left and mutual generation is the forward number;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth's virtue is generation; the River Chart turns left in forward generation;

sentences.zh: 洛書右轉，而相剋為逆數。

translations.literal: the Luo Writing turns right and mutual overcoming is the reverse number.
translations.idiomatic: the Luo Writing turns right in reverse overcoming.

sentences.zh: 一順一逆，位所由易也。

translations.literal: One forward and one reverse—positions change thereby."
translations.idiomatic: Forward and reverse explain the change of positions."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「既順何以逆？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "If forward, why also reverse?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked why there is reverse if there is forward.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「孤陽不生，獨陰不成。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Solitary yang does not generate; solitary yin does not complete."
translations.idiomatic: " He said solitary yang does not generate and solitary yin does not complete.

sentences.zh: 河圖自北而東，順以相生，木火土金水，就流行言；

translations.literal: The River Chart from north to east proceeds by generation—wood, fire, earth, metal, water—speaking of circulation;
translations.idiomatic: The River Chart from north to east generates wood, fire, earth, metal, water in circulation;

sentences.zh: 洛書自北而西，逆則相剋，上下四方中，就對待言。

translations.literal: the Luo Writing from north to west proceeds by overcoming—above, below, four directions, center—speaking of opposition.
translations.idiomatic: the Luo Writing from north to west overcomes in opposition above, below, four sides, and center.

sentences.zh: 既五數在中，縱橫皆十五矣，惟剋乃所以生也。

translations.literal: Since five is in the center, vertically and horizontally all sum to fifteen; only overcoming is how generation occurs.
translations.idiomatic: With five in the center all lines sum to fifteen; only overcoming enables generation.

sentences.zh: 陰陽交則生變，變則生生不易。

translations.literal: When yin and yang interact, change is born; through change generation is unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and yang interacting birth change; change makes generation unceasing.

sentences.zh: 」上又​​問曰：「洪範九疇，皇建有極，謂人參三才，此說是乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor again asked: "In the Hong Fan's nine categories, the emperor establishes the supreme norm—does the saying that man joins the three powers hold?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked whether man joining the three powers fits the Hong Fan's supreme norm.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「自天地開闢以來，賴有聖人，原治而不原亂者，天地之心；

translations.literal: " He replied: "Since Heaven and Earth opened, we rely on sages; Heaven and Earth's mind seeks order, not disorder;
translations.idiomatic: " He said sages seek order, not disorder, which is Heaven and Earth's mind;

sentences.zh: 有治而不能無亂者，天地之數。

translations.literal: yet there can be order and cannot be without disorder—that is Heaven and Earth's number.
translations.idiomatic: yet order cannot exist without disorder—that is Heaven and Earth's number.

sentences.zh: 數至則生聖人，撥亂而返之治，裁成輔相，以左右民，則聖人建極會極歸極之功也。

translations.literal: When the number arrives a sage is born, sets disorder aright, forms and assists to guide the people—that is the sage's work of establishing, meeting, and returning to the norm.
translations.idiomatic: When the number matures a sage restores order and guides the people—establishing, meeting, and returning to the norm.

sentences.zh: 聖人既能撥亂而返之治，始副天地長治之心，此人參三才之說，實理也，亦實事也。

translations.literal: Once the sage can set disorder aright, he fulfills Heaven and Earth's mind of long order; this saying that man joins the three powers is real principle and real fact."
translations.idiomatic: Restoring order fulfills Heaven and Earth's long-order mind—man joining the three powers is real principle and fact."

sentences.zh: 」上頗嘉美之。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor greatly approved.

sentences.zh: 遷順天府府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Governor of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遷右副都御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he became Right Vice Censor.

sentences.zh: 再遷兵部督捕侍郎，以病告歸，未及行，卒。

translations.literal: Again transferred to Vice Minister of War in charge of bandit suppression; he asked to return on illness but died before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to bandit-suppression vice minister of war; he asked to retire ill and died before leaving.

sentences.zh: 三禮初師事孫奇逢，及在海寧，從黃宗羲遊，官京師，有所疑，必貽書質宗羲。

translations.literal: Sanli first studied under Sun Qifeng; at Haining he followed Huang Zongxi; in the capital whenever he doubted he wrote to ask Huang.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Sun Qifeng, followed Huang Zongxi at Haining, and wrote to Huang with doubts in the capital.

sentences.zh: 斅宋趙抃故事，旦晝所為，夜焚香告天，家居及在海寧，皆建告天樓。

translations.literal: Following Song Zhao Bian's example, he reported his daytime deeds to Heaven by incense at night; at home and in Haining he built Report-to-Heaven towers.
translations.idiomatic: Following Zhao Bian, he burned incense nightly to report his deeds and built Report-to-Heaven towers.

sentences.zh: 聖祖重道學，嘗以之稱三禮云。

translations.literal: The Kangxi emperor valued the Way and once praised Sanli thus.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi valued the Way and praised Sanli thus.

sentences.zh: 王士禎，字貽上，山東新城人。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen, courtesy name Yishang, was a native of Xincheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen, courtesy name Yishang, came from Xincheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 幼慧，即能詩，舉於鄉，年十八。

translations.literal: Clever in youth, he could compose poetry at once; he passed the provincial examination at eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Clever as a boy, he wrote poetry early and passed the provincial exam at eighteen.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，成進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi 12 he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 授江南揚州推官。

translations.literal: Appointed investigating censor of Yangzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Yangzhou investigating censor in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 侍郎葉成格被命駐江寧，按治通海寇獄，株連眾，士禎嚴反坐，寬無辜，所全活甚多。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Ye Chengge was ordered to stay at Jiangning and investigate the Tonghai pirate case; many were implicated; Shizhen strictly applied counter-charges, lenient to the innocent, and saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Chengge's Tonghai pirate case implicated many; Shizhen counter-charged strictly and spared many innocents.

sentences.zh: 揚州鹺賈逋課數万，逮系久不能償，士禎募款代輸之，事乃解。

translations.literal: Yangzhou salt merchants owed tens of thousands in arrears and were long detained unable to pay; Shizhen raised funds to pay for them and the matter was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Salt merchants owed tens of thousands; Shizhen raised funds to pay and freed them.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，總督郎廷佐、巡撫張尚賢、河督硃之錫交章論薦，內擢禮部主事，累遷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi Governors Lang Tingzuo, Zhang Shangxian, and River Director Zhu Zhixi jointly recommended him; he was promoted within to Rites clerk and rose to Revenue division director.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 3: recommended by Lang Tingzuo, Zhang Shangxian, and Zhu Zhixi; promoted to Rites clerk and Revenue director.

sentences.zh: 十一年，典四川試，母憂歸，服闋，起故官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he conducted the Sichuan examination, returned on his mother's mourning, and after mourning resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he examined Sichuan, mourned his mother, then resumed office.

sentences.zh: 上留意文學，嘗從容問大學士李霨：「今世博學善詩文者孰最？

translations.literal: The emperor valued literature and once casually asked Grand Secretary Li Hui: "Who today is most erudite and skilled in poetry and prose?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Grand Secretary Li Hui who was most erudite in poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 」霨以士禎對。

translations.literal: " Hui answered with Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui named Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 復問馮溥、陳廷敬、張英，皆如霨言。

translations.literal: Asked again about Feng Pu, Chen Tingjing, and Zhang Ying—all answered as Hui had.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Feng Pu, Chen Tingjing, and Zhang Ying—all agreed.

sentences.zh: 召士禎入對懋勤殿，賦詩稱旨。

translations.literal: Shizhen was summoned to audience in the Hall of Earnest Diligence; his poem pleased the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the Hall of Earnest Diligence, his poem pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 改翰林院侍講，遷侍讀，入直南書房。

translations.literal: Changed to Hanlin Lecturer, promoted Reader, and entered the Southern Studios.
translations.idiomatic: Made Hanlin Lecturer, then Reader, and entered the Southern Studios.

sentences.zh: 漢臣自部曹改詞臣，自士禎始。

translations.literal: A Hanlin official promoted from a ministry post began with Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin promotion from a ministry post began with Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 上徵其詩，錄上三百篇，曰御覽集。

translations.literal: The emperor requested his poems; three hundred were recorded as the Imperially Reviewed Collection.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor collected three hundred poems as the Imperially Reviewed Collection.

sentences.zh: 尋遷國子監祭酒，整條教，屏餽遺，獎拔皆知名士。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Director of the Directorate of Education; he set regulations, refused gifts, and promoted renowned scholars.
translations.idiomatic: As Education Director he set rules, refused gifts, and promoted renowned scholars.

sentences.zh: 與司業劉芳喆疏言：「漢、唐以來，以太牢祀孔子，加王號，尊以八佾、十二籩豆。

translations.literal: With Vice Director Liu Fangzhe he memorialized: "Since Han and Tang, the great offering has sacrificed to Confucius, adding a kingly title and honoring with eight rows and twelve vessels."
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Fangzhe he said Han and Tang used the great offering for Confucius with kingly honors.

sentences.zh: 至明嘉靖間，用張璁議，改為中祀，失尊崇之意。

translations.literal: In Ming Jiajing, following Zhang Cong's proposal, it was changed to a middle offering, losing the meaning of honor.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Jiajing's middle offering lost proper honor.

sentences.zh: 禮：祭從生者。

translations.literal: Rites say sacrifice follows the living.
translations.idiomatic: Rites say sacrifice follows the living.

sentences.zh: 天子祀其師，當用天子之禮樂。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven sacrifices to his teacher, he should use the Son of Heaven's ritual music.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven should use imperial ritual music for his teacher.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「自明去十哲封爵，稱冉子者凡三，未有辨別。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Since Ming removed the Ten Sages' titles, three called Master Ran were not distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said Ming left three Master Rans undistinguished.

sentences.zh: 宋周敦頤等六子改稱先賢，位漢、唐諸儒之上，世次殊有未安，宜予釐定。

translations.literal: Song's Zhou Dunyi and five others were changed to called sages and placed above Han and Tang Ru—generations are unsettled and should be clarified."
translations.idiomatic: Song's six sages above Han and Tang Ru need clarification."

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「田何受易商瞿，有功聖學，宜增祀。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Tian He received the Changes from Shang Qu—merit to sage learning—should be added to sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: " Tian He should be added to sacrifice for transmitting the Changes.

sentences.zh: 鄭康成注經百餘萬言，史稱純儒，宜复祀。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotated the classics in over a million words; histories call him a pure Ru—should be restored to sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan, called a pure Ru, should be restored to sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 二十三年，遷少詹事。

translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he became Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 命祭告南海，父憂歸。

translations.literal: Ordered to sacrifice to the southern sea; he returned on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to sacrifice to the southern sea; he mourned his father.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，起原官，再遷兵部督捕侍郎。

translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he resumed office and again became bandit-suppression vice minister of war.

translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he moved to Revenue.

sentences.zh: 命祭告西嶽西鎮江瀆。

translations.literal: Ordered to sacrifice to the western peak, western marchmount, and river gods.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to sacrifice to the western peak, marchmount, and rivers.

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he became Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會廷議省御史員額，士禎曰：「國初設御史六十，後減為四十，又減為二十四。

translations.idiomatic: Debating censor cuts, he said the founding sixty were cut to forty, then twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 天子耳目官，可增不可減。

translations.idiomatic: The emperor's eyes and ears may increase, not decrease."

sentences.zh: 」卒從士禎議。

translations.literal: " In the end Shizhen's view was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizhen's view prevailed.

translations.literal: Transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He became Minister of Justice.

translations.idiomatic: As Vice Censor he won reduction in the Yang Cheng case.

translations.idiomatic: As Revenue Vice Minister he won reductions in three cases but applied the law to Hengyang heterodox Xiao Ruying.

translations.idiomatic: " Changed to suspended execution and approved.

translations.idiomatic: Shizhen won favor through poetry and enjoyed great grace.

translations.idiomatic: In year 43 he was dismissed over Wang Wu and Wu Qian.

translations.idiomatic: Wu was a Works artisan who bought the rank of sub-prefect;

translations.idiomatic: Qian was a medical officer who beat a debtor to death collecting a debt.

translations.literal: Referred again to the Three Judicial Offices for strict examination, both were sentenced to death; Qian's entrustment of Justice clerk Ma Shitai was also exposed; Shizhen was stripped for favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Retried, both were sentenced to death; Qian's bribe to Ma Shitai appeared; Shizhen was stripped for favoritism.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，上眷念諸舊臣，詔復職。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year, remembering old ministers, an edict restored his post.
translations.idiomatic: In year 49 an edict restored him.

sentences.zh: 五十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he died.

sentences.zh: 明季文敝，諸言詩者，習袁宗道兄弟，則失之俚俗；

translations.literal: At the end of Ming literature was decadent; those who spoke of poetry followed the Yuan brothers and became vulgar;
translations.idiomatic: Late Ming poetry followed the Yuan brothers into vulgarity;

translations.literal: followed Zhong Xing and Tan Youxia and became cramped;
translations.idiomatic: followed Zhong and Tan into cramped mannerism;

sentences.zh: 斅陳子龍、李雯，軌轍正矣，則又失之膚廓。

translations.literal: emulated Chen Zilong and Li Wen and the track was correct but became empty and broad.
translations.idiomatic: emulated Chen Zilong and Li Wen into correct but empty breadth.

translations.literal: Shizhen's natural endowment was high and learning extremely broad; with brothers Shilu and Shihu he devoted himself to poetry, taking spiritual resonance alone as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and learned, with brothers Shilu and Shihu he took spiritual resonance as poetry's standard.

sentences.zh: 取司空圖所謂「味在酸鹹外」、嚴羽所謂「羚羊掛角，無跡可尋」，標示指趣，自號漁洋山人。

translations.literal: Taking Sikong Tu's "flavor beyond sour and salt" and Yan Yu's "antelope hanging by its horn, no trace to seek," he marked his aim and styled himself the Fisherman of Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He took Sikong Tu and Yan Yu as models and styled himself the Fisherman of Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 主持風雅數十年。

translations.literal: He presided over elegant letters for several decades.
translations.idiomatic: He led literary fashion for decades.

sentences.zh: 同時趙執信始與立異，言詩中當有人在。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhixin at first disputed him, saying poetry must have a person in it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhixin first disputed him, saying poetry must have a person.

sentences.zh: 既沒，或詆其才弱，然終不失為正宗也。

translations.literal: After his death some criticized his talent as weak, yet he never ceased to be regarded as orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: After death some called his talent weak, yet he remained orthodox.

sentences.zh: 士禎初名士禛，卒後，以避世宗諱，追改士正。

translations.idiomatic: Originally Shizhen, posthumously changed to Shizheng to avoid the Shizong taboo.

translations.idiomatic: " Posthumous Wensuian was granted.

translations.idiomatic: All offices' books and records were to be changed uniformly.

translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Five Classics, was tranquil and broad, and loved landscape.

translations.idiomatic: He drank and joked with friends all day, yet his conduct was pure and strict.

sentences.zh: 特工製舉文。

translations.idiomatic: At Shuntian's exam Xu Qianxue picked him from the rejected pile.

translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 12 he topped both exams, became compiler and Daily Lecturer.

translations.idiomatic: Kangxi ordered his Supreme Ultimate treatise and essays and summoned him to lecture on the Great Learning.

translations.idiomatic: Shizu's unfinished Filial Piety exegesis was entrusted solely to Tan.

translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became Tutor.

translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became Court Lecturer.

translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he again examined Shuntian.

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he asked leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he asked leave and went home.

translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he resumed office and soon became Reader.

translations.idiomatic: In year 24 the emperor tested the Hanlin; Tan ranked second and became Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 尋擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Grand Secretary.

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he again took leave and built a house on the Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he took leave again and built on the Western Hills.

translations.idiomatic: He collated classic commentaries and studied the histories.

translations.idiomatic: Dahai only created the national script—one art."

sentences.zh: 」持不可。

translations.literal: " He held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: " He opposed it.

translations.idiomatic: Yongding River work opened purchase precedents for circuit and prefecture posts.

translations.idiomatic: Tan opposed purchasing posts; Zheng Weizi said many students from Jiang-Zhe tested with false registration.

sentences.zh: 請盡發原籍肄業。

translations.literal: Please send them all back to study in their home districts."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to send them all home to study."

sentences.zh: 」菼曰：「京師首善地，遠人鄉化，方且聞風慕義而來。

translations.idiomatic: " Tan said the capital is the chief seat and distant men come drawn by righteousness.

translations.idiomatic: Expelling all for a few bad ones would empty the Directorate—not proper.

translations.literal: Weizi's words were wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Weizi was wrong.

sentences.zh: 」事得寢。

translations.literal: " The matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was dropped.

translations.idiomatic: In year 39 he lectured at the Classics Colloquium, became Minister of Rites, and taught bachelors.

translations.idiomatic: In year 41 he asked to resign to compile; kept and given the plaque Steadfast in Classical Learning, Adorning Great Works.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，再稱疾，上不悅，敕仍留原任。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he again pleaded illness; the emperor was displeased and ordered him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In year 42 he pleaded illness again; the emperor was displeased and kept him.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，再疏乞退，仍不允。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he again memorialized asking to retire—still not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In year 43 he again asked to retire—still denied.

translations.literal: That autumn he died; mourning followed rites.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he died; mourning followed rites.

translations.idiomatic: Famous for literature, in court he set moral tone, spoke boldly, and kept faith to the end.

translations.idiomatic: On leave again Qianxue had been dismissed and headed the Dongting book bureau.

translations.idiomatic: Governor Fu Lata framed Qianxue for a great case; friends withdrew.

translations.idiomatic: Tan visited daily and cleared the false charge, and it stopped.

translations.literal: When he returned to office the emperor treated him generously and once said: "Han Tan is talent of the realm, fine bearing, honest in audience."
translations.idiomatic: Restored, the emperor said Han Tan was realm talent with fine bearing and honest audience.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「菼學問優長，文章大雅，前代所僅有。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Tan's learning is outstanding and writing grand—rare since former ages."
translations.idiomatic: " He also said Tan's learning and grand writing were rare since former ages.

sentences.zh: 所撰擬能道朕意中事。

translations.literal: What he drafted could express what was in my mind."
translations.idiomatic: His drafts expressed the emperor's mind."
