sentences.zh: 下廷臣議，有言阿山與有連，妄語罪當死。

translations.literal: Referred to the court; some said Ashan was connected and reckless speech deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: Debated; some said Ashan was connected and reckless speech deserved death.

sentences.zh: 菼謂縱有連，情私而語公。

translations.literal: Tan said even if connected, the feeling was private but the words public.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said even if connected, feeling was private but words public.

sentences.zh: 忌者增益其語入告，上由是疏菼。

translations.literal: Jealous men added to his words in reports; the emperor therefore grew distant from Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies exaggerated his words; the emperor grew distant.

sentences.zh: 及再謝病，詔責其教習庶吉士，每日率以飲酒多廢學；

translations.literal: When he again asked leave on illness, an edict rebuked his teaching of bachelors—daily leading them in drinking and neglecting study;
translations.idiomatic: Again ill, he was rebuked for teaching bachelors to drink and neglect study;

sentences.zh: 九卿集議，不為國事直言，惟事瞻徇。

translations.literal: the Nine Ministers deliberated—not speaking frankly on state affairs, only showing favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: the Nine Ministers said he did not speak frankly, only showed favoritism.

sentences.zh: 菼意不自得，病甚，飲不輟，至卒。

translations.literal: Tan was ill at ease, grew very ill, drank without stopping, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Distressed, very ill, he drank without stopping until death.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十七年，高宗諭獎「菼雅學績文，湛深經術。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Qianlong Gaozong praised: "Tan's elegant learning and accumulated writing, profound classical mastery."
translations.idiomatic: Qianlong 17 Gaozhong praised Tan's elegant learning and profound classics.

sentences.zh: 所撰制義，清真雅正，開風氣之先，為藝林楷則」。

translations.literal: The examination essays he wrote are pure, correct, and elegant, opening the age's tone and a model for the literary world."
translations.idiomatic: His examination essays were pure and elegant, a model for the literary world."

sentences.zh: 追諡文懿。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Wenyi was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous Wenyi was granted.

sentences.zh: 子孝嗣，舉人；

translations.literal: His son Xiaosi, a provincial graduate;
translations.idiomatic: Son Xiaosi was a provincial graduate;

sentences.zh: 孝基，進士，官編修，菼卒，奉母不出十餘年。

translations.literal: Xiaoji, a jinshi and compiler; when Tan died he served his mother without leaving for over ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji, jinshi and compiler, served his mother over ten years after Tan's death.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，召修明史。

translations.literal: Early in Yongzheng he was summoned to compile the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yongzheng he was summoned to compile the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 書成，移疾歸，年九十而終。

translations.literal: When the book was done he asked leave on illness and returned; he died at ninety.
translations.idiomatic: When done he retired ill and died at ninety.

sentences.zh: 湯右曾，字西厓，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Tang Youhui, courtesy name Xiya, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Youhui, courtesy name Xiya, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi; became a bachelor and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi 27 jinshi; bachelor and compiler.

sentences.zh: 出典貴州試。

translations.literal: He went out to conduct the Guizhou examination.
translations.idiomatic: He examined Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed Censor of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: In year 39 he became Revenue Section Censor.

sentences.zh: 兩廣總督石琳疏言瓊州生黎以文武官吏婪索，激而為亂。

translations.literal: Liangguang Governor Shi Lin memorialized that Qiongzhou raw Li were provoked to revolt by greedy civil and military officials.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Shi Lin said Qiongzhou Li revolted because officials extorted them.

sentences.zh: 上遣侍郎凱音布、學士邵希穆按治。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Vice Minister Kaiyinbu and Academician Shao Ximu to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Kaiyinbu and Shao Ximu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 右曾疏言：「揭帖言瓊州文武官往黎峒採取沈香、花梨致生釁，石琳及巡撫蕭永藻、提督殷化行平時絕不覺察，且黎亂在上年，遲且一載，始行題報，掩飾欺隱，請嚴加處分。

translations.literal: Youhui memorialized: "A placard says Qiongzhou officials entered Li ravines to collect aloeswood and rosewood, provoking trouble; Shi Lin, Governor Xiao Yongzao, and Commander Yin Huaxing never noticed; the Li revolt was last year yet reported only after a year—concealment and deception—please punish severely."
translations.idiomatic: Youhui said officials collecting timber provoked the Li, leaders concealed a year-old revolt—punish severely.

sentences.zh: 」石琳等皆下吏議。

translations.literal: " Shi Lin and others were all referred for official deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Lin and others were all referred for punishment.

sentences.zh: 四十年，疏請刊頒政治典訓及御製文集。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he memorialized asking to print and distribute the Political Canon and the imperial collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: In year 40 he asked to print the Political Canon and imperial writings.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，轉戶部掌印給事中。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was transferred to Revenue Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 41 he became Revenue Chief Censor.

sentences.zh: 初，以私錢多，改錢制輕小，使私鑄無所利，顧仍不止。

translations.literal: At first, because private coin was abundant, coinage was made light and small so private casting would not profit—yet it still did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Private coin was abundant; light small coin was meant to stop private casting—it did not.

sentences.zh: 上令仍鑄大錢，下廷臣議，改鑄大錢，其舊鑄小錢，期二年銷毀。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered large coin cast again; the court debated casting large coin and destroying old small coin within two years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered large coin; debate set two years to destroy small coin.

sentences.zh: 右曾疏言：「改大錢宜遵聖諭，若毀小錢則民間必驚擾。

translations.literal: Youhui memorialized: "Changing to large coin should follow the holy edict; destroying small coin would surely disturb the people."
translations.idiomatic: Youhui said large coin should follow the edict; destroying small coin would disturb the people.

sentences.zh: 且戶、工二部存錢八十四萬串，若議銷毀，工料耗折甚多。

translations.literal: Moreover Revenue and Works stored eight hundred forty thousand strings; if destruction is debated, labor and materials waste greatly."
translations.idiomatic: Revenue and Works held 840,000 strings; destruction would waste labor and materials."

sentences.zh: 且二年中鑄出新錢不過一百萬串，豈能遍及各省？

translations.literal: Moreover in two years newly cast coin would not exceed one million strings—how could it reach every province?"
translations.idiomatic: New coin in two years could not exceed one million strings—how reach every province?"

sentences.zh: 新錢無多，舊錢已毀，恐私鑄更繁，錢法愈壞。

translations.literal: Little new coin, old coin already destroyed—fear private casting would increase and the currency worsen.
translations.idiomatic: Little new coin with old destroyed would worsen private casting.

sentences.zh: 古者患錢重，則改輕而不廢重；

translations.literal: Anciently when coin was too heavy, they made it light without abolishing the heavy;
translations.idiomatic: When coin was heavy they made light without abolishing heavy;

sentences.zh: 患錢輕，則改重而不廢輕：使子母相權而行。

translations.literal: when too light, they made it heavy without abolishing the light: let mother and child coins balance each other.
translations.idiomatic: when light they made heavy without abolishing light—mother and child coins balance.

sentences.zh: 新鑄重錢，每串作銀一兩；

translations.literal: Newly cast heavy coin, each string valued at one tael of silver;
translations.idiomatic: New heavy coin: each string at one tael silver;

sentences.zh: 舊鑄輕錢作七錢：並聽行使。

translations.literal: old light coin at seven mace: both permitted in circulation.
translations.idiomatic: old light coin at seven mace: both circulate.

sentences.zh: 積久大錢流通，小錢自不行矣。

translations.literal: In time heavy coin would circulate and small coin naturally cease.
translations.idiomatic: In time heavy coin would circulate and small coin cease.

sentences.zh: 」疏再下廷臣議，定新錢每重一錢四分，舊錢並行勿禁，如右曾議。

translations.literal: " The memorial was again debated; new coin was fixed at one mace four fen weight, old coin permitted in parallel without prohibition—as Youhui proposed.
translations.idiomatic: " Debated again; new coin at 1.4 mace, old parallel—as Youhui proposed.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，提督河南學政。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was Educational Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 44 he was Henan Educational Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，巡撫汪灝疏言右曾取士公明。

translations.literal: At term's end Governor Wang Hao memorialized that Youhui selected scholars fairly.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end Governor Wang Hao said he selected scholars fairly.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，遷奉天府府丞。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was transferred to Vice Governor of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 48 he became Vice Governor of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In year 49 he became Director of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 五十年，轉太常寺卿、通政使。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he was transferred to Director of Imperial Sacrifices and Transmission Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 50 he became Sacrifices Director and Transmission Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，擢翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was promoted Hanlin Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 51 he became Hanlin Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 52 he became Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 尚書富寧安、陳鵬翮皆廉辦有威棱，右曾貳之，銳意文案，糾剔是非。

translations.literal: Ministers Funing'an and Chen Penghe were both efficient and formidable; Youhui assisted them, keen on documents, correcting right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting efficient ministers Funing'an and Chen Penghe, he keenly corrected documents.

sentences.zh: 選人或挾大力以相要，必破其機紐，俾終不獲選。

translations.literal: Candidates who relied on powerful backers to demand favor—he always broke their schemes so they never obtained selection.
translations.idiomatic: He broke powerful candidates' schemes so they never obtained selection.

sentences.zh: 由是乾進射利者，皆叢怨於吏部，而富寧安往蒞西師，鵬翮任事久，見知於上深，莫可搖動，遂爭為浮言撼右曾。

translations.literal: Therefore those who advanced by intrigue all resented Personnel; Funing'an went to the western army and Penghe had long served and was deeply known to the emperor and could not be shaken—they competed in slander to shake Youhui.
translations.idiomatic: Intrigue resented Personnel; powerful ministers slandered him.

sentences.zh: 六十年，命解右曾侍郎，仍專領掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he was ordered relieved of the vice ministry and to head the Hanlin chancellorship alone.
translations.idiomatic: In year 60 he was relieved of the vice ministry but kept the Hanlin chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year he died.

sentences.zh: 右曾少工詩，清遠鮮潤。

translations.literal: Youhui was skilled at poetry from youth—clear, distant, fresh, and moist.
translations.idiomatic: Youhui wrote clear, distant, fresh poetry from youth.

sentences.zh: 其後師事王士禎，稱入室。

translations.literal: Later he studied under Wang Shizhen and was called a true indoor disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied under Wang Shizhen as a true disciple.

sentences.zh: 使貴州後，風格益進，鍛鍊澄汰，神韻泠然。

translations.literal: After serving in Guizhou his style advanced further—refined, clarified, spiritual resonance cool and clear.
translations.idiomatic: After Guizhou his style refined further with cool spiritual resonance.

sentences.zh: 右曾朝熱河行在，上命進所為詩，​​右曾方詠文光果，即以進上。

translations.literal: Youhui attended the emperor at the Rehe traveling palace; ordered to present his poems, he was just composing on the wenguang fruit and presented that to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At Rehe ordered to present poems, he presented one on the wenguang fruit.

sentences.zh: 上為和詩，有句曰「叢香密葉待詩公」，右曾自定集，遂取是詩冠首。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a matching poem with the line "dense fragrance and close leaves await the poetry lord"; Youhui's collected works take that poem as the first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor matched with "dense fragrance and close leaves await the poetry lord"; Youhui made it his collection's first poem.

sentences.zh: 論曰：方藹、荃、杜訥以文學直內廷，其結主知，尤在於廉謙。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Fangai, Quan, and Du Ne, through literature serving directly in the inner court, won their rulers' trust especially through frugality and humility.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment: Fangai, Quan, and Du Ne won favor through literature and frugality.

sentences.zh: 元珙、三禮議禮各申其所見，有當於經指。

translations.literal: Yuangong and Sanli debated rites each stating his view—both hit the classics' aim.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangong and Sanli debated rites each to the classics' aim.

sentences.zh: 士禎以詩被遇，清和粹美，蔚為一代正宗。

translations.literal: Shizhen was favored through poetry—clear, harmonious, pure, and beautiful, towering as the orthodox master of an age.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen was favored through poetry—clear and pure, orthodox master of an age.

sentences.zh: 菼於文亦然，久而論定，並邀補諡，增文字之重。

translations.literal: Tan was the same in literature; in time judgment settled, and he too received a supplementary posthumous title, adding weight to letters.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tan was the same in literature; in time judgment settled, and he too received a supplementary posthumous title, adding weight to letters.

sentences.zh: 右曾師事士禎，繼以詩被遇。

translations.literal: Youhui studied under Shizhen and likewise was favored through poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Youhui studied under Wang Shizhen and likewise won favor through poetry.

sentences.zh: 論者謂自明弘治、正德以後一百五十年，而文章复在臺閣，為聖祖崇儒右文之效雲。

translations.literal: Commentators say that from Ming Hongzhi and Zhengde onward, after a hundred fifty years, literature again resided in the court cabinets—the effect of the Kangxi emperor's honoring Ru learning and promoting writing.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators say that after a hundred fifty years since Ming Hongzhi and Zhengde, literature again flourished in the court cabinets—the fruit of the Kangxi emperor's honoring Confucian learning and promoting letters.
